sketch: Instead of treating the percolation walk as a random unitary channel and analysing its asymptotics, purify the randomness coherently. Instance: a 4-site cycle (periodic 1D chain) with a coin qubit and 4 position states (2 qubits), plus one ancilla qubit per edge, 4 total, each prepared in cos(t)|0>+sin(t)|1> with t chosen so P(edge open)=p. Registers: position (2 qubits), coin (1 qubit), edge ancillas (4 qubits). One step: (1) Hadamard coin; (2) a controlled shift, where each edge ancilla controls whether the walker crosses that edge (open) or is reflected and flips its coin (closed), compiled as multi-controlled gates on position, coin and the relevant edge ancilla; (3) the same ancillas are NOT reused. For T steps, use fresh ancillas per step (4T ancillas), which gives exactly the independent per-step random edge configuration of the dynamic percolation model. Tracing out the ancillas yields the mean channel rho -> sum_omega p(omega) U_omega rho U_omega^dagger. The built circuit is the full unitary on walker plus ancillas. For tiny T (1 or 2) it is verified by simulating the circuit and comparing the reduced walker state with the explicit average over edge configurations. The asymptotic behaviour (the paper's random-unitary-map asymptotics) is probed only by increasing T numerically, not derived; the output is the walker's position distribution after tracing out the ancillas. This is a different family because it uses Stinespring dilation with coherent ancilla randomness and finite-T simulation, rather than spectral or asymptotic analysis of the random unitary map.
